title: Board resolutions that waive competition for a named party
question: How often does the Board of Supervisors itself waive competitive bidding for one named firm or organization, and for whom?
finding: 27 Board files from 2014 to November 2026 waive competitive bidding or approve sole-source dealing with a named party; the amounts stated in their titles add up to $504.1 million. 17 date from 2022 or later, the largest of those being Low Income Investment Fund ($67.7 million).
how: Board of Supervisors files, 2014 to November 2026, whose title speaks of waiving competitive bidding or solicitation, an exemption from the competitive bidding policy, or sole-source negotiation or agreement. Grant acceptances and lawsuit settlements are left out. The amount is the one stated in the title; several leases and negotiations state none.
limits: These are the waivers that needed a public vote; the far larger number approved inside departments is in the other screens. Titles were read by pattern, so a waiver worded differently is missed. A waiver to negotiate with one developer for a public site follows a published policy. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
